title: Off-Policy Evaluation of Ranking Policies under Diverse User Behavior

problem.claim: Accurately evaluating ranking policies from logged data is difficult because inverse propensity scoring has high variance in ranking settings with large action spaces.

gap.claim: Existing ranking estimators use a single universal user-behavior assumption, which can cause excessive bias and variance when user behavior is diverse.

contributions.claim: The work formulates off-policy evaluation for ranking systems with user behavior that can vary by user context.
It proposes Adaptive IPS (AIPS), an estimator that can be unbiased under complex user behavior and has minimum variance among IPS-based unbiased estimators.
It develops a data-driven procedure for identifying an appropriate user-behavior model to minimize AIPS mean squared error.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Extensive experiments reportedly show significant empirical accuracy improvement for off-policy evaluation of ranking systems under diverse user behavior.

narrative_sequence.summary: Ranking interfaces are widespread, creating interest in evaluating ranking policies from logged data.
IPS is unbiased and consistent in general but becomes highly inaccurate for ranking because of high variance, while prior estimators rely on universal behavior assumptions.
The work models diverse user behavior and introduces AIPS for this setting.
AIPS is reported to be unbiased under complex user behavior and minimum-variance among IPS-based unbiased estimators.
A data-driven model-selection procedure is developed, and experiments report significant accuracy improvements.

source_observation.claim: Using one universal behavioral assumption for all users can produce excessive bias and variance when behavior varies across contexts.

interpretation.claim: Evaluation methods may need to represent heterogeneous behavior rather than force a single population-wide model.

application.claim: For logged ranking-policy evaluation, consider context-dependent behavior models and data-driven selection among them.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify when the proposed behavior models or data-driven procedure may fail or be inappropriate.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the datasets, baselines, metrics, or experimental settings.
The abstract does not provide the conditions or proof details for the unbiasedness and minimum-variance claims.
The abstract does not describe the data-driven behavior-model identification procedure.
